description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/latlon/rules/central_D2_lat_zero_grad_bc driven by problems/latlon_diffusion_meridional_zero_grad.esm. The problem file is loaded once per resolution with the loader-API metaparameter binding (esm-spec 9.7.6 binding site 4) — NLAT is the open metaparameter (NLON is edge-closed at 8; the solution is zonally symmetric), and the problem's dlat_deg observed and inlined lat coordinates use the NLAT name, so the geometry follows each rebinding automatically. The ladder NLAT = 17/33/65/129 halves the spacing dlat = 180/(NLAT-1) exactly each step; `n` records the interval count NLAT-1 = 16/32/64/128 so the order fit uses the true refinement ratio 2. Manufactured steady solution u* = cos^4((pi/180) lat) with an exact diffusion source (derivation and the O(dlat^2) pole-supercompatibility argument in the problem file — a plain cosine eigenmode would collapse the order to 1 on this node-coincident pole grid); the recorded errors at t=0.2 are pure interior + compatible-pole O(dlat^2) truncation drift.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no makearray lowering / simulator

python._doc: Pinned so Python temporal truncation is negligible against the spatial goldens: LSODA at 1e-12/1e-14 handles the stiff diffusion sweep and agrees with the Julia Tsit5 reference to well under the error_vs_golden tolerance on every resolution, where a loose explicit RK method would leave a temporal residue comparable to the spatial error.
